idea-plugin.name: Commit Line Splitter
idea-plugin.description:
Split a Git commit line by line, right from the Git Log.

IntelliJ's built-in Extract Selected Changes to Separate Commit… can only move whole files. Commit Line Splitter goes one step further: pick exactly which added and removed lines of a file should move to a new commit, and leave the rest in the original commit.

How to use

  1. Open Git → Log and select a commit on your current branch.
  2. In the commit's changed files, right-click a file and choose Split Lines to Separate Commit… (directly below the built-in extract action).
  3. Tick the lines that should move. Use the gutter checkboxes, the per-change header, or Space for the caret or selection.
  4. Enter a message for the new commit and confirm. The new commit is placed directly after the original one.

Safe by design

  • The working tree and index are never touched, so it works even with uncommitted changes.
  • Conflicts are impossible: later commits keep their exact content and are only re-parented.
  • Original authors, author dates and message encodings are preserved byte-for-byte, including CRLF line endings and a missing final newline.
  • You are warned before rewriting commits that are already on a remote branch.
  • You can undo with one click from the notification.

Compatibility

  • Supported: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1, 2026.2 and 2026.3 (builds 261–263.*). Verified with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier on 2026.1.5 and 2026.2.4.
  • Not supported: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 and older, and 2027.1 and newer until a compatible update is released.
  • Other JetBrains IDEs 2026.x with the bundled Git plugin (e.g. PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand) may work, but they are not tested.

Limitations

  • Requires linear history between the commit and HEAD (no merge commits).
  • Renamed or moved files and binary files are not supported.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1

  • Fixed: "Access from Event Dispatch Thread (EDT) is not allowed" error after splitting or undoing. The repository and Git Log are now refreshed in the background.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: line-level splitting of commits from the Git Log, with hunk toggles, keyboard support and undo.
